definition.en-US: A set of written rules, with its own words and grammar, that tells a computer what to do.

analogy.en-US: Like a recipe written in a shared cooking language, which any cook who knows that language can follow.

definition.en-US: The software a program needs while it runs, such as the interpreter that reads and carries out its code.

analogy.en-US: Like the stage, lights and crew that a play needs on the night it is performed.

definition.en-US: A ready-made piece of code, written by someone else, that your program uses instead of writing that part itself.

analogy.en-US: Like buying a ready-made sauce for a dish instead of making it from scratch.

definition.en-US: A written description of the job you want done, the rules the AI must follow and how you will check the result.

analogy.en-US: Like the order ticket a waiter gives the kitchen, which says what the table wants and what must not be changed.

definition.en-US: A folder of its own inside a project that holds the packages for that project, separate from packages used elsewhere on your computer.

analogy.en-US: Like a separate toolbox for each job, so that one job's tools do not get mixed up with another's.

definition.en-US: A ready-made set of tools and rules for building a certain kind of program, such as a web app.

analogy.en-US: Like a flat-pack furniture kit, where the parts and instructions are already designed so you do not cut the wood yourself.

definition.en-US: A problem where something that worked before stops working after a change.

analogy.en-US: Like repainting one wall of a room and finding that the light switch on another wall no longer works.

definition.en-US: One fixed input together with the result you expect from it, used to compare two versions fairly.

analogy.en-US: Like tasting two batches of soup made from the same recipe and the same amount of salt, so that the difference is easy to judge.

definition.en-US: The list of files and lines a Python program was running when it failed, printed with the error at the end.

analogy.en-US: Like the trail of footprints left in the snow that shows the route someone took before they fell.
